summary: Summation No. 21 covers June 1947, the first month of the Katayama Cabinet (Social Democrat-led tripartite coalition formed 1 June) and the first Diet session under the new Constitution (opened 23 June). Part II reports the eight-point emergency economic program of 11 June, the New Life Movement, party conventions, the purge of newspaper and broadcasting figures, the Ministry of Home Affairs abolition decision, crime and fire statistics, atrocity trials, and Far East Tribunal testimony on the Soviet phase and German-Japanese relations. Part III gives May production data for coal, iron and steel, chemicals, machinery and textiles; power, transport and communications; labor unions, disputes and wages; trade; food rationing and price rises; finance; and property control. Part IV covers nutrition surveys, disease rates, repatriation, education conferences, textbooks, religion and media. Historians will find detailed statistics and primary-source texts of Cabinet and Diet statements.
highlights: Prime Minister Tetsu Katayama's Cabinet announced an eight-point emergency economic program on 11 June, covering food collection, official price and wage revision, anti-inflation finance, production priorities, employment, exports and selective state control; Communists and Liberals criticized it.

The Diet opened 23 June with Speaker Komakichi Matsuoka presiding in place of the Emperor, who attended as a 'guest'; the two Houses' presiding officers had earlier denied the Government's right to set the length of the session.

On 20 June the Cabinet launched a seven-point 'People's Movement for the Construction of a New Japan', drafted by Education Minister Tatsuo Morito and Junzo Sasamori; on 27 June it decided to recommend abolishing the Ministry of Home Affairs.

The Government announced standards on 27 June for purging ultranationalists from newspapers, radio and publishing, screening officers of publications over 30,000 circulation; seven Councillors were removed and 508,941 persons screened since 4 January.

The International Military Tribunal for the Far East closed the Russian phase (Tanaka, Deane, Yalta Agreement evidence) and opened the Pacific phase with German witnesses Stahmer and Kretschmer, then recessed 23 June to 4 August.
Bank of Japan notes in circulation reached 136,320,000,000 yen on 30 June; the national debt stood at 286,866,035,074 yen on 31 May; official rayon, camphor, sugar and milk prices rose sharply.
Coal output in May was 2,103,500 metric tons, 206,500 under quota; pulp and paper hit postwar highs, cotton cloth reached 62,357,000 square yards, and sulfuric acid output hit a record 127,928 tons.

Japanese repatriated in June totaled 61,170 (44,317 from Soviet areas); May nutrition surveys showed Tokyo caloric intake falling from 1,921 to 1,792 per day, while no major strikes occurred and union membership reached 5,445,493.

sections.title: Front matter
sections.summary: Cover for Summation No. 21 (June 1947), table of contents for Parts I-IV, and list of 118 charts, maps and graphs with Map of Japan.

sections.title: Part I: General
sections.summary: Condensed digest of the month: no SCAP organizational change, Katayama Cabinet policies, war crimes actions, industrial output, labor, finance, and health, education and media developments.

sections.title: Organization Under SCAP
sections.summary: States that there was no change in the non-military organization of General Headquarters, SCAP, during June.

sections.title: Political Activities
sections.summary: Summarizes the Diet term dispute, the eight-point economic program, the 20 June New Life Movement, ordered apprehension of 76 suspects and Tribunal testimony on Russia and Pearl Harbor.

sections.title: Economic Activities
sections.summary: Digest of May output in mining, heavy industry, textiles and power, plus the industrial production index charts, labor developments, food distribution (41 percent imported), finance and property control.

sections.title: Social Activities
sections.summary: Digest of nutrition survey declines, hospitals (3,224), 61,170 repatriates, textbook printing (44,410,823 copies), teacher screening, Christian influence in Government and information programs.

sections.title: Part II: Political
sections.summary: Covers the new Diet and Katayama Cabinet, party conventions, the purge, public safety statistics, and war crimes investigations, trials and Far East Tribunal proceedings.

sections.title: Government and Politics
sections.summary: Reports the Diet's assertion of control over session length, Councillor backgrounds, Katayama's 11 June eight-point program with party and press reaction, the Home Affairs abolition, new Finance Minister Kurusu and the purge.

sections.title: The Diet
sections.summary: Speaker Matsuoka and President Matsudaira reject a Government three-week extension; 21 standing committees organized; 23 June opening ceremony and Emperor's rescript; occupational profile of 250 Councillors.

sections.title: Political Developments
sections.summary: Full text of the eight-point emergency program, Nosaka and Ono criticisms, press comment, official discipline, New Life Movement text, and Democratic, Liberal and Social Democratic Party conventions.

sections.title: The Central Government
sections.summary: Cabinet recommends abolishing the Ministry of Home Affairs on 27 June; Takeo Kurusu replaces Shotaro Yano as Finance Minister; new Legislation Bureau and Cabinet Secretariat officials.

sections.title: The Emperor and the Constitution
sections.summary: Emperor's 12-day Kansai tour from 4 June after the first joint press interview with the Empress; periodical commentary on popular sovereignty and pacifism in the new Constitution.

sections.title: The Purge
sections.summary: 508,941 persons screened since 4 January; seven Councillors removed; 2,490 prefectural assembly candidates screened; 27 June standards for purging newspaper, radio and publishing leaders.

sections.title: Public Safety
sections.summary: Closure of black-market eating places from 1 July, 161,153 criminal offenses in April, rail casualties down 13 percent, new Tokyo police chief Toga, prison population 72,342 and April fire losses.

sections.title: Legal and War Crimes
sections.summary: Japanese courts gain jurisdiction over theft of Occupation property; 1,917 atrocity cases on hand; 255 defendants tried; Tribunal hears Tanaka, Deane, Stahmer and Kretschmer before recessing 23 June.

sections.title: International Prosecution of War Criminals
sections.summary: Russian phase closes with Tanaka, Kozuki, Deane and Matsumura testimony and the Yalta Agreement; Pacific phase opens with German witnesses denying advance knowledge of Pearl Harbor.

sections.title: Part III: Economic
sections.summary: May statistics for agriculture, mining, industry, power, communications, labor, trade, rationing, finance and property control, with price rises, the cement shortage and record chemical and paper output.

sections.title: Agriculture and Fisheries
sections.summary: Tenant priority to buy land occupied on 23 November 1945; livestock slaughter up; 350 whales from Bonin Islands whaling; 1,500,000 yen for agricultural libraries; plans ordered for 1947-48 antarctic whaling.

sections.title: Forestry and Mining
sections.summary: Log output 544,824,000 board feet; May coal 2,103,500 tons, 206,500 under quota; stockpiles 754,600 tons; petroleum 17,669 kiloliters; April mineral table with tungsten up 143 percent.

sections.title: Heavy Industries
sections.summary: Coke 154,320 tons; aluminum 1,197 tons; housing starts up 67 percent; cement shortage cuts public works; sulfuric acid record 127,928 tons; industrial machinery 418,505,000 yen; textile machinery.

sections.title: Manufacturing
sections.summary: Fats and oils 198 percent of April; paper 36.5 percent above April; glass, electrical goods, trucks 777, bicycles 16,178 (postwar high), leather, handicrafts, sewing machines up 55 percent.

sections.title: Textile Industries
sections.summary: Cotton cloth peak 62,357,000 square yards though yarn fell to 26,545,000 pounds; 891,647 bales of CCC cotton imported; raw silk 10,749 bales; rayon filament record; first Australian wool shipments.

sections.title: Transportation and Public Utilities
sections.summary: Truck operating ratio 64.8 percent; 292,919,131 rail passengers; power generation 2,988,794,000 kWh with restrictions only in Chugoku, Shikoku and Kyushu; gas plants at 37 percent of capacity.

sections.title: Communications
sections.summary: International Telecommunications Company liquidation, Tokyo-Manila service from 1 June, 14,000 new telephones, 625 radio stations, Tsugaru Strait cable, equipment output and 731 research projects.

sections.title: Labor
sections.summary: Committees draft Labor Ministry Bill; unions total 5,445,493 members; April disputes fell to 57; no major June strikes; wages up about 30 percent since January; coal recruitment and public works employment.

sections.title: Labor Relations
sections.summary: Central Labor Relations Committee first annual report; 81 percent of union members under collective agreements; steel tube strike of 18,000 averted 1 June; metal mining and railway wage settlements.

sections.title: Imports and Exports
sections.summary: Food imports flat; cotton fabric shipped to seven new markets including Aden and Nigeria; first postwar pearls to the United States; storage batteries to China; tabulated April and May cargoes.

sections.title: Rationing and Price Control
sections.summary: Rice collection 4,349,177 tons (103 percent of quota); 29 days' government staple stocks; ration delays near five days; wheat price up 121 percent; rayon, camphor, sugar, milk and fares raised.

sections.title: Finance
sections.summary: Banque de l'Indochine opens; Bank of Japan notes 136,320,000,000 yen; Security Coordinating Liquidation Committee formed 18 June; liquidation proceeds 2,740,204,000 yen; first pay-as-you-go tax declarations.

sections.title: Property Control and Reparations
sections.summary: Neutral and Allied property 890,553,000 yen; German assets 783,129,000 yen; 155 dissolved organizations; 151 holding-company applications approved; control companies designated; reparations delegations visit machine-tool plants.

sections.title: Part IV: Social
sections.summary: Public health, nutrition and welfare statistics, repatriation, education conferences and teacher screening, religion, arts, press, radio, film, theater and music, ending with the Map of Japan.

sections.title: Public Health and Welfare
sections.summary: May nutrition survey (Tokyo calories 1,792), disease rates, 3,224 hospitals, penicillin 341,620,000 units, 87 narcotics violators, 2,763,333 relief recipients, production fund loans and 61,170 repatriates.

sections.title: Education, Culture and Media of Expression
sections.summary: Courses-of-study conferences from 16 June, 2,643 educators purged, 44,410,823 textbooks printed, Katayama's Christian influence, press comment on the economy, 601,504 film attendance and a Map of Japan.
